title: SGM-PINN: Sampling Graphical Models for Faster Training of Physics-Informed Neural Networks
problem: Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) require large mini-batches and training datasets for parameterized problems, causing slow convergence and high computational costs.
motivation: Improving PINN training efficiency enables faster deployment of physics-informed models for scientific computing applications.
method: The approach builds a dependency map of training samples—a probabilistic graphical model showing which samples relate to each other. It groups samples into clusters based on these dependencies and determines which clusters will help most during training. Rather than sampling randomly, it focuses on high-value clusters and uses error metrics to identify regions that need more coverage.
key_novelty: Using probabilistic graphical model decomposition to identify training-sample dependencies and create importance-weighted sampling clusters.
contributions: Graph decomposition-based importance sampling framework for PINN training acceleration
Method to identify conditional dependencies through probabilistic graphical models
Robustness metric integrated with residual losses for adaptive region-specific sampling
3× speedup compared to prior state-of-the-art sampling methods
